solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Young woman on crack finally quitting: it takes spirit (4,5)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B
indicatorNotes.finally: take only the final letter of 'quitting'

blocks.note: have a crack = have a shot, an attempt

annotation.surface: A young woman kicks a crack habit, and it takes real spirit to do it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crack' and 'spirit' both pose as drugs-and-willpower words; crack is an attempt, and spirit is the drink the glass holds.
annotation.definitionFit: A shot glass is a small glass that holds a single measure of spirits.

annotation.definitionNote: both definitions are verbs in the third person: he rifles, he sacks

blocks.note: to sack a town is to plunder, rifle through it
to axe a worker is to sack them

annotation.surface: A list of weapons: guns and hatchets.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like plural nouns from an armoury; each is a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: Sacks means both plunders (rifles) and dismisses from a job (axes).

indicatorNotes.Sadly: sadly = badly, in a sorry state, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: hewing = cutting, as with an axe

annotation.surface: Someone regrets not cutting something that is flying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as a noun or adjective; it is a verb, and the answer's word breaks fall in different places from the pieces' own breaks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain idiom: birds shot on the wing are hit in mid-flight, so the phrase means airborne.

entries.clue: Resistance, following Asterix perhaps, regularly belittles petty tyrant (9)

indicatorNotes.following: following means coming after, so R is placed after the pieces the clue names next

blocks.note: Asterix is the comic-book Gaul; 'perhaps' marks him as an example

annotation.surface: The Resistance follows Asterix in mocking a small-time despot, as the Gauls did the Romans.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets up occupied France, which suits the answer: a Gauleiter was a Nazi district governor, now any officious petty tyrant.
annotation.definitionFit: Gauleiter, once a Nazi regional chief, is used for any overbearing minor official.

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: the letters are presented wrongly, out of order

annotation.surface: The deadly significance of some law has been misrepresented.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A statute is a law passed by a legislature, which in Britain is an Act of Parliament.

entries.clue: Enthusiastic reception of proxy governor replacing head of state (8,7)

indicatorNotes.replacing: GOV goes in where the N was
indicatorNotes.head of: the first letter of NATION is the one swapped out

blocks.note: a stand-in acts as a proxy
GOV is an informal clipping of governor, the boss or guv'nor
a state = a nation; its head N is dropped for GOV, leaving ATION

annotation.surface: A deputy governor, standing in for the head of state, gets a warm welcome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Proxy governor' reads as one official; it is two pieces, STAND-IN and GOV, and 'head of state' is not a president but the N of NATION.
annotation.definitionFit: A standing ovation is an audience rising to applaud, the most enthusiastic of receptions.

entries.clue: Starts to stimulate idle mate with exercise (3-2)

indicatorNotes.Starts to: take the first letter of each of the next two words

blocks.note: first letters of Stimulate and Idle
to tup is to mate, of a ram

annotation.surface: Someone tries to rouse a lazy partner by getting them to exercise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a partner; it is the verb, and TUP is the farmyard word for a ram mating.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the sit-up, lifting the trunk from lying flat, is one of the commonest gym exercises.

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, A on B puts A above B

annotation.surface: Money paid on account to buy spices.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Money on account' reads as a bookkeeping phrase; the pieces simply stack, SUM over AC.
annotation.definitionFit: Sumac is a tart red spice made from dried berries, common in Middle Eastern cooking.

entries.clue: Secret society in China and a Pacific archipelago (5)

blocks.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society

annotation.surface: A list of two exotic things: a Chinese secret society and a Pacific island group.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' looks like part of the definition, but it is the last letter; the definition is just 'Pacific archipelago'.
annotation.definitionFit: Tonga is a kingdom made up of about 170 islands in the South Pacific.

entries.clue: Big beast, in pain, died in Barnet (9)

indicatorNotes.in: ACHY and D go inside PERM

blocks.note: d = died, as in family trees
Barnet is rhyming slang (Barnet Fair) for hair, and a perm is a hairdo

annotation.surface: A large animal, in agony, died in Barnet, a district of north London.
annotation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the London borough; it is Cockney rhyming slang, Barnet Fair = hair, so a hairstyle: PERM.
annotation.definitionFit: A pachyderm is a thick-skinned animal such as an elephant or rhino.

indicatorNotes.from: the answer is taken from inside the next words

blocks.note: reversal indicator: the hidden letters read right to left

annotation.surface: A garment from Mauritius sent back politely.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a tactful return of an unwanted purchase; 'tactfully' is there only for its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A catsuit is a close-fitting one-piece garment covering body, arms and legs.

entries.clue: Almost entirely crazy, disregarding current calendar (7)

indicatorNotes.Almost: drop the last letter of ALL
indicatorNotes.disregarding: leave out the I for current

blocks.note: MANIAC without I, the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: Someone nearly out of their mind ignores the current calendar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Almost entirely' reads as one phrase meaning nearly; 'Almost' is the cut and 'entirely' is ALL. 'Current' is not recent but I, the physics symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly calendar with dates, tides and other data.

entries.clue: English explorer is close to his dog (5)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of 'is' is its last letter

blocks.note: a Peke is a Pekingese dog; 'his' belongs to the surface

annotation.surface: An English explorer is devoted to his dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is close to' reads as emotional closeness; it takes the last letter of 'is'. John Hanning Speke found the source of the Nile at Lake Victoria.
annotation.definitionFit: John Hanning Speke was a Victorian English explorer of East Africa.

entries.clue: Doubt about record probed by University College trustee (9)

indicatorNotes.about: about in the sense of turned about, facing the other way, so IF is written backwards
indicatorNotes.probed by: UC goes into DIARY, as a probe goes in

blocks.note: an if is a doubt, as in 'no ifs or buts'
a diary is a record of events
its initials, placed inside DIARY: D(UC)IARY

annotation.surface: A university college trustee has doubts about some record under investigation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning'; it turns IF round.
annotation.definitionFit: A fiduciary is someone who holds property in trust for another: a trustee.

entries.clue: Tearful Chinese communist’s second to be purged (5)

indicatorNotes.to be purged: remove the named letter, as a party purges a member

blocks.note: a Maoist follows Mao Zedong; the ’s is 'has'
the second letter of MAOIST, removed

annotation.surface: A Chinese communist's deputy is due for a purge and is close to tears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads as a deputy, apt with 'purged'; it is the second letter of MAOIST.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyes that well up go damp, so the adjective for damp eyes also means close to tears.

indicatorNotes.framing: MATE goes round CHINA like a frame round a picture

blocks.note: another chum: china is rhyming slang (china plate = mate)

annotation.surface: A friend sets up another friend as part of a conspiracy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Framing' suits the plot of the surface, a stitch-up; it is the container. 'Another' means another chum, and china = mate is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the verb goes with machination, a crafty scheme, so it means to scheme.

indicatorNotes.fake: a fake is a made-up version, so the letters are made up anew

annotation.surface: Anybody is able to pretend to be hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pain' looks like physical hurt; it is a pain in the sense of a nuisance.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial sense: a person or thing that irritates is called a pain, meaning a nuisance.

entries.clue: Shortened long canon in The Four Seasons (4-5)

indicatorNotes.Shortened: cut the last letter off YEARN

blocks.note: to long = to YEARN, less its last letter
a round is a canon, a song where voices enter in turn

annotation.surface: A long canon cut short within Vivaldi's The Four Seasons.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals point to Vivaldi, but the definition means all four seasons, the whole year. 'Long' is the verb, yearn.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful paraphrase: covering all four seasons means lasting the whole year through.

entries.clue: Reportedly understands element of chess or bridge (9)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: as reported, spoken, so the sound counts

annotation.surface: Someone apparently grasps a key part of chess or bridge, the card game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chess or bridge' reads as two games; bridge is the definition, the part of glasses resting on the nose.
annotation.definitionFit: The nosepiece of a pair of glasses is the bridge between the lenses.

indicatorNotes.hot: hot = stolen or wild, so the letters are disturbed

annotation.surface: Smoke rising from garlic oil heating in a pan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' reads as what hot oil gives off; it is a noun for something you smoke.
annotation.definitionFit: A cigarillo is a small thin cigar, a smoke.

indicatorNotes.before: before in the sense of ahead of, so the fool is placed ahead of the time of day

blocks.note: a mug is a fool, an ass
am = before noon; 'before' also places it

annotation.surface: A mug of tea in the morning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is the cup of the surface, but here it is a fool. 'Before noon' does double duty: it orders the pieces and AM means before noon.
annotation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea from the Indian state of that name.

indicatorNotes.Retired: retired = gone back, so ROMANI is turned round

blocks.note: the Romani are the Gypsy people

annotation.surface: A retired American gives thanks to a Gypsy sweetheart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired American' reads as a pensioner; 'Retired' turns round the Gypsy at the far end of the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: From Italian innamorata, 'enamoured woman': a woman one loves, a sweetheart.

indicatorNotes.cycling: letters go round, moving from the front to the back

blocks.note: IDE moves from the front of IDEAS to the back

annotation.surface: Someone takes a fancy to going off on a bike ride.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancies cycling' reads as wanting a bike ride; 'Fancies' is a noun, ideas.
annotation.definitionFit: Aside means away or to one side, as in 'put aside'.

annotation.surface: An attack on the experts now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attack' reads as a verb; it is the noun, an onset being an assault.
annotation.definitionFit: A slightly old-fashioned sense: the word once meant a military assault, the rush of an attacking force.

blocks.note: the RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

annotation.surface: The navy's gunners fall back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' sits in a naval scene with gunners, but it is the adjective: fleet of foot, fast.
annotation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective is literary for quick-moving, as in fleet of foot: a plain synonym.

indicatorNotes.cuts: OP cuts into DRS, going inside it

blocks.note: DR = doctor, plus the S of ’s

annotation.surface: A doctor's practice is cutting back on medicines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor’s surgery' reads as a GP's practice, the British word for a doctor's consulting rooms; here surgery means an operation, which cuts into the doctor's abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Drops, for the eyes or ears, are a kind of medication.

entries.clue: Clothing of adolescent offspring under discussion (2,5)

indicatorNotes.Clothing of: the outside of a word, as clothes are, gives its outer letters

annotation.surface: What teenage children wear is a topic of family debate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' reads as garments; it is the outside of 'adolescent'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the point at issue is the one being argued over, so the phrase means up for debate.

indicatorNotes.supply: read as the adverb of supple: bent, flexibly arranged

annotation.surface: A regular stock order has not arrived.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as a noun, a stock; it is the adverb 'supplely', bending the letters of ROUTINE. 'Delivered' is birth, not a parcel.
annotation.definitionFit: In utero means in the womb, a baby not yet born.

indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is a part of the following words

annotation.surface: A prospective section of a keynote lecture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prospective' fits the sense of 'elect' after a title, as in 'president-elect': chosen but not yet in office.
annotation.definitionFit: Elect after a title means chosen and about to take office, so prospective.

entries.clue: Tenor consumed by endless fondness for female attire (4,5)

indicatorNotes.consumed by: T is swallowed by the other word, going inside it
indicatorNotes.endless: drop the last letter of TENDRESSE

blocks.note: tendresse = fondness (from French), losing its final E

annotation.surface: A tenor is eaten up by an endless love of women's clothing.
annotation.walkthrough: Tendresse is a borrowed word for tender feeling; minus its final E it takes in T to become TENT DRESS.
annotation.definitionFit: A tent dress is a loose, wide dress that flares from the shoulders.
